confirmedIssues: Wrong CVE identifier copied into English; primary record is unrelated to JWT.
JWT format and cookie transport are compared as if mutually exclusive.
JWT defined only as private-key signed; signature validation alone presented as sufficient and self-issuer implied.
JWT expiry assumed mandatory, revocation impossibility and performance degradation asserted without design conditions or measurement.
HttpOnly treated too broadly as an XSS remedy; session IDs described as intrinsically safe and instant revocation ignores distributed caching.
Refresh-token storage and fixed example lifetime described as universal, and refresh state equated with every-request lookup.
Internal network trust, one-time reset URLs and OAuth access/ID token roles need explicit security boundaries.

primaryReferences.readScope: Abstract; section 3 overview; section 4 and 4.1 claim optionality; 4.1.4 expiration excerpt. Not a whole-RFC review.
primaryReferences.finding: JWT is a claims representation using JWS/MAC and/or JWE, not necessarily private-key signed. The generic format does not require every registered claim.

primaryReferences.readScope: Sections 1, 2.1, 2.8, 3.1-3.3, 3.8-3.12 excerpts; not all cryptographic guidance or referenced papers.
primaryReferences.finding: Algorithm selection and key binding must follow application rules; none and RSA/HMAC confusion are distinct implementation failures. Signature checking alone does not establish intended issuer, recipient or token use.

primaryReferences.readScope: Fetched and read CNA English description and cveMetadata from the primary CVE list using Invoke-RestMethod; browser fetch failed.
primaryReferences.finding: This record concerns Datto ALTO/SIRIS restore mount point ACLs, unrelated to JWT alg:none. Do not silently substitute CVE-2015-9235 for a none vulnerability: RFC 8725 cites that ID for RSA/HMAC confusion.

primaryReferences.readScope: Abstract and section 3 implementation note, including self-contained versus reference tokens and back-end revocation coordination.
primaryReferences.finding: Self-contained token revocation is a system design tradeoff with state/coordination costs; not categorically impossible. A refresh-token revocation alone does not magically invalidate all locally validated access tokens.

primaryReferences.readScope: Sections 2.2.2 and 4.14.1-4.14.2 including replay protection and expiration; not all OAuth attack sections.
primaryReferences.finding: Refresh issuance is risk-based. Public clients receiving refresh tokens require sender constraints or rotation; access-token validation may remain local even when refresh grant management has state.

primaryReferences.readScope: Cookie Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and name-prefix sections.
primaryReferences.finding: HttpOnly prevents script reading of cookies but hostile same-origin scripts can still cause authenticated requests. SameSite is a CSRF defense layer; session IDs also need theft, fixation and lifecycle protections.

primaryReferences.readScope: Local Storage section and adjacent storage warnings; not all browser API guidance.
primaryReferences.finding: Web Storage is readable by origin scripts; sessionStorage lifetime does not prevent XSS exfiltration.

primaryReferences.readScope: Sections 1.4-1.5 and 7 validation excerpts only. Earlier implicit/password grant descriptions were not treated as current recommendations; RFC 9700 updates security advice.
primaryReferences.finding: OAuth access-token formats vary; JWT is not mandated for every access token. Refresh tokens are optional and distinct from resource-server access tokens.

primaryReferences.readScope: Section 2 ID Token definition, claims and signing/encryption excerpts.
primaryReferences.finding: An OIDC ID Token is a JWT about end-user authentication for a client. Do not conflate it with a resource API access token.

primaryReferences.readScope: Reset-token requirements and URL token section.
primaryReferences.finding: A reset token needs expiry, user binding and one-use invalidation. Choosing JWT format alone does not make a URL one-time.
